title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 118 (Minutes of proceedings of general meeting, meeting of Board of Directors and other meeting and resolutions passed by postal ballot)

content.overview: Every company shall cause minutes of the proceedings of every general meeting of any class of shareholders or creditors, every resolution passed by postal ballot, and every meeting of its Board of Directors or of every committee of the Board, to be prepared and signed in the prescribed manner and kept within thirty days of the conclusion of every such meeting or of the passing of resolution by postal ballot in books kept for that purpose with their pages consecutively numbered. Secretarial Standards notified under section 118(10) are mandatory to the extent applicable. Duly kept minutes are evidence of the proceedings.
content.glance: Minutes of covered meetings and postal-ballot resolutions must be prepared, signed and kept within thirty days; applicable Secretarial Standards must be followed.
content.study:
## Section 118 — Minutes

**What must be recorded.** Minutes of general meetings, meetings of classes of shareholders and creditors, Board meetings, committee meetings, and resolutions passed by postal ballot must be prepared, signed and kept in the relevant minute books. The general statutory period for entering minutes is thirty days.

**Secretarial Standards.** Standards approved and notified under section 118(10) are mandatory to the extent applicable (including SS-1 for Board meetings and SS-2 for general meetings).

**Evidentiary effect.** Minutes duly kept under the section are evidence of the proceedings. Minutes do not cure defects in notice, quorum or voting.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.body: Record minutes for covered meetings and postal-ballot resolutions within thirty days in consecutively numbered books.

sections.heading: Secretarial Standards
sections.body: Comply with notified Secretarial Standards under section 118(10) to the extent applicable.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.body: Duly kept minutes are evidence of proceedings but do not cure invalid meeting defects.

hypotheticals.question: Do accurate minutes validate a meeting that lacked quorum?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Minutes are evidence of proceedings but do not cure defects in notice, quorum or voting.

misconceptions.trap: Treating minutes as curing an invalid meeting.
misconceptions.correction: Minutes evidence what occurred; they do not independently validate defective proceedings.
